## rebar-debug RCA — shared ticket-store lock (2026-08-27)

Problem
The documentation plan review and its follow-up correction comment encountered the shared ticket-store write lock. Earlier descriptions of the holder as unrelated, stale, orphaned, or safe to kill were unsupported and are retracted.

Proven mechanism
PID 11145 was an intentional, live quiet-window barrier started by another active Codex session for a review-event transplant. It held rebar._store.lock.write_lock across signal.pause until that session explicitly released it. The 30-second timeout and zero retries in the holder invocation bounded acquisition only; they were not a lease on the held context.

Proof
- Owner transcript rollout-2026-08-23T10-25-30-01a02fa7-f2c2-7203-b778-be740ceb2111.jsonl declared the barrier before launch, reported QUIET_LOCK_READY, and later recorded session 48697 exiting.
- OS evidence tied PID 11145 to that worktree and live Codex parent and showed FD 3 on the canonical .ticket-write.lock.
- The plan-review sidecar showed the three canonical acquisition passes and failed after 181 seconds while that exact PID was still live. The review continued because src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:60-107 defines the sidecar as best effort.
- The correction comment remained alive for approximately the same bounded window and landed no event. Its terminal stderr was not collected, so no exact error text is inferred.
- After explicit release, PID and FD ownership disappeared, .ticket-write.lock.d was absent, and a real search completed in 3.88 seconds without a lock warning.
- Scratch runtime experiment: a separate helper held an isolated dual-window lock. A canonical waiter with scaled one-second passes exhausted three passes in 4.361 seconds and named the live helper; run_ensures made one pass and skipped in 1.037 seconds. Normal helper exit made busy false, immediate reacquisition succeeded, .lock.d was absent, and only the expected zero-byte lock file remained.
- Separate scratch CLI experiment: with a pre-mounted tracker and its write lock actively held, an ordinary search returned in 0.149 seconds. The three observed 60-second read stalls were concurrent first-use worktree mounts entering the idempotent ensure sweep before the tracker symlink existed, not ordinary reads taking the write lock.

Alternatives rejected
A stale mkdir leg, failed release, orphan, self-deadlock, and version-skew explanation conflict with the live distinct holder PID, controlled normal release, clean post-release state, and absence of relevant source changes between holder revision 9c0776d and current 0c8e302.

Classification
Intended behavior, not a rebar defect. docs/concurrency.md:263-313 specifies exclusive dual-window writes, roughly 180 seconds of canonical acquisition retries, then loud failure. src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:147-198 specifies a single bounded attempt and skip; the plan-review sidecar is explicitly best effort. A requirement to queue beyond those budgets or provide a leased quiet-window primitive would be new behavior, not a repair to this incident.

No code, documentation, or tests were changed, and no shared process was signalled or killed.
